title: Normal shared latest-pointer advancement invalidates a previous day's exact HK publication chain
source_identity_basis: Local supplied owner sources and in-progress candidate after sources; these identities do not attest deployed or loaded Mac bytes.

observed_source_identities.role: exact HK child candidate after; host target ops/macos_research_panel_daily.py

facts: The publisher reads shared assets/hk_security_master/latest.json, changes entries[trade_date], then atomically writes the complete latest object.
Publishing the next date changes latest bytes while retaining the previous date entry and its date-specific artifact/manifest/receipt.
Selects latest.entries[requested_trade_date], resolves that run's manifest, receipt and artifact, and checks date/run/SHA/safety/row contracts.
It does not pin the entire latest file hash. A valid unrelated next-date entry does not by itself invalidate previous-date master readback.
For a newer through_date, writes a content-identified panels/{through_date}-{sha-prefix} artifact and manifest, then advances shared panel_latest.json.
The new panel records parent_panel_sha256 and the normal next-date path does not overwrite the previous dated panel artifact.
For through_date <= current_max, returns the current panel manifest/SHA after verifying the requested date exists in it; it does not reselect the older exact panel.
Loads the current panel through panel_latest.json and verifies its panel artifact hash.

faulty_binding_chain.fact: Lines 614 and 630 add the full live panel_latest.json and master latest.json to artifact_refs as HK_PANEL_LATEST_POINTER and HK_SECURITY_MASTER_LATEST_POINTER; _file_ref records current whole-file bytes and SHA.

Rechecks every artifact reference against its current path without excluding mutable pointer roles. Changed size raises HK_PUBLICATION_CHAIN_ARTIFACT_MISSING; changed digest raises HK_PUBLICATION_CHAIN_ARTIFACT_SHA_MISMATCH.

Also dereferences current panel_latest and requires it to link the previous chain's panel manifest/max date. The master branch reads the current global pointer and selects the requested date entry. Merely skipping whole-pointer SHA checks does not resolve the panel branch.

Any cached-chain read failure returns CANNOT_CONFIRM, failed_stage FINAL_READBACK and public reason HK_PUBLICATION_CHAIN_POINTER_INVALID. The code explicitly refuses to downgrade it to cache miss. Return occurs before new chain_id/start evidence or any capture/publisher invocation.
Calls the gate's exact reader; the same failure returns false and invalidates yesterday's lane-ready fast path.

static_cross_day_scenario: Day 1: original owners publish a valid 20261008 master/panel and gate seals a READY chain including current shared latest pointer bytes.
Day 2: original master publisher adds a valid 20261009 entry and/or original panel updater advances panel_latest to a valid 20261009 panel.
No Day 1 immutable artifact needs to change for the Day 1 artifact_refs comparison to fail.
Direct original master loading of 20261008 remains allowed by its entry-level contract; the new gate's 20261008 exact reader fails at the global-pointer comparison.
The candidate gate does not automatically republish historical membership/master in response to that failure.

cache_miss_boundary.conclusion: Not a harmless cache miss and not evidence of observed historical data pollution.
facts: The current early failure prevents a new chain or publisher call; no old immutable run overwrite is reached on this path.

Changing the exception handling to cache miss alone still does not produce a valid historical rebind: the original panel updater returns the newer current manifest, while ops.ensure_hk_security_master._read_verified_hk_panel_authority at lines 97-140 requires the live pointer/authority identity and panel_max_date == requested old date.

The already-sealed exact capture/run/artifact identities must remain the basis of any eventual solution. This review does not authorize republishing historical eligibility, rewriting old chains or bypassing original owner checks.

impact_limits: Previous-day exact-chain verification, cache reuse and HK lane-ready fail after ordinary next-day shared pointer progress.

A new target date uses its own hk_publication/{target}/latest.json; no dependency on the previous chain was found in this entry, so this finding alone does not establish that Day 2 execution is blocked.
Previous master artifacts can still pass the original exact-date master reader. This review does not establish failure of every manager historical plan or reader.
The failure can break two-day acceptance even when all previous immutable run bytes remain unchanged.
No runtime reproduction, canary, Mac command, test execution or natural-day observation was performed by this reviewer.
